brief.topic: The Water That Quietly Holds a Piece of Wood

s01: A piece of wood rests partly inside the water.
The water is quietly carrying its weight.
Where does that upward support come from?
Imagine holding the block completely underwater.
Water pressure increases with depth.
The bottom feels a stronger upward push than the downward push on top.
The sideways pushes cancel.
What remains is an upward force.
Now imagine replacing the block with water, without changing its shape.
The surrounding water pushes on the same boundary.
That little parcel of water can rest in balance.
So the upward support must match the weight of the parcel.
Put the block back.
The support is the weight of the water that would occupy its submerged space.
This is the idea behind buoyancy.
A floating block settles until that support equals its own weight.
For this uniform wood, imagine a density sixty percent that of water.
Sixty percent of its volume sits below the surface.
A denser block needs to displace more water.
At eighty percent density, it sits lower.
We are ignoring waves and surface tension in this simple model.
Floating is a quiet balance between what is there and the water it makes room for.

scenes.narration:
A piece of wood rests partly inside the water. The water is quietly carrying its weight. Where does that upward support come from?

Imagine holding the block completely underwater. Water pressure increases with depth. The bottom feels a stronger upward push than the downward push on top. The sideways pushes cancel. What remains is an upward force.

Now imagine replacing the block with water, without changing its shape. The surrounding water pushes on the same boundary. That little parcel of water can rest in balance. So the upward support must match the weight of the parcel.

Put the block back. The support is the weight of the water that would occupy its submerged space. This is the idea behind buoyancy. A floating block settles until that support equals its own weight.

For this uniform wood, imagine a density sixty percent that of water. Sixty percent of its volume sits below the surface. A denser block needs to displace more water. At eighty percent density, it sits lower. We are ignoring waves and surface tension in this simple model. Floating is a quiet balance between what is there and the water it makes room for.
